why_lead: Tesla meets all three tests on this date's evidence: the card shows the stock at 272.04 dollars, down 29.10 percent over 20 sessions and 10.16 percent over five, which is a sharp drawdown rather than a quiet name. The crowd is repeating a simple robotaxi-and-robots case, with Morgan Stanley's 430 dollar target, Musk's tenfold profit claim and Cathie Wood's endorsement in circulation, and the attention is visible in owner anger, leveraged-ETF losses and record zero-day options. The brand and political risk gives the institutional disagreement a clear shape, so the piece can say where the bulls and bears actually differ.
why_smaller: XRP is the only non-equity trade with a surge on this date, up 11.67 percent over five sessions, with reserve-related retail attention, though the reserve premium is already fading.
IonQ is the clearest quantum pure play, down 46.11 percent over 20 sessions, with a steady stream of retail-oriented headlines about the sector's breakthroughs and a dilution-sensitive funding setup.

Rheinmetall is the non-AI, European rearmament trade, up 47.98 percent over 20 sessions and 17.76 percent over five, with defence headlines in Europe and the Polish retail press calling the sector hot.
considered_not_chosen: Palantir (PLTR): an analyst call on Pentagon cuts popped the stock about 5 percent in one session [n2670], but the card shows +1.17 percent in the prior session and only +0.79 percent over 20 sessions, so there is no sustained move behind the headline.
Sandisk (SNDK): retail is excited about the relisted stock and an analyst's upside call [n5751], but the card has no 20-session return for it, so the price half of the test cannot be measured.

Nebius (NBIS): it crashed on Monday [n5747] and is down 11.11 percent over 20 sessions, but there is no dated catalyst and the attention is generic AI-infrastructure enthusiasm rather than a trade of its own.

Super Micro (SMCI): up 45.77 percent over 20 sessions after a filing that cleared the deadline [n2378]; it is a relief move on a filing, with no simple crowd thesis that would carry several days of attention.

Gold and gold miners: gold is up 2.22 percent over 20 sessions and the '$3,000' framing [n7740] has no price surge behind it, so it is too thin for a lead, and it is already covered as a materials sentiment point.

Nuclear reactor names (OKLO, SMR, NNE): deep 20-session drawdowns, with Oklo down 32.68 percent, but the headlines in this window are policy items; the fuel chain is used instead as an underowned theme.
Bitcoin miners (CIFR, IREN, RIOT, MARA): sharp 20-session drawdowns with no retail-attention headlines in this window, so there is no crowd story to write about.
Oil and OPEC+: WTI is down 6.70 percent over 20 sessions on the output hike [n7833], which is clear price evidence, but no retail-attention headline exists for crude, so it fails the attention test.
Mixue (Hong Kong IPO): the debut jumped 43 percent [n3370] and set a record for retail subscriptions, but that is a one-off listing event rather than a narrative the crowd repeats across days.
